## Solution

**Setup.** Place rectangle $ABCD$ with $A=(0,0)$, $B=(36,0)$, $C=(36,15)$, $D=(0,15)$, so $AB=36$, $BC=15$. The center of the circle (radius 1) must lie at least distance 1 from every side, so it is uniformly distributed over the region $\mathcal{R} = [1,35]\times[1,16]$, with area $34\cdot 13 = 442$.

**Diagonal and distance.** Diagonal $AC$ lies on the line through $(0,0)$ and $(36,15)$, i.e. $5x - 12y = 0$. The distance from a point $(x,y)$ to this line is
$$d = \frac{|5x-12y|}{\sqrt{25+144}} = \frac{|5x-12y|}{13}.$$
The circle does **not** touch $AC$ iff $d > 1$, i.e. $|5x-12y| > 13$. So we need the area of the complement of the strip $|5x-12y|\le 13$ within $\mathcal{R}$.

**Computing the strip area.** The condition $|5x-12y|\le 13$ is equivalent to
$$\frac{5x-13}{12} \le y \le \frac{5x+13}{12},$$
giving an unclipped vertical width of $\frac{26}{12}=\frac{13}{6}$.

Find clipping boundaries within $x\in[1,35]$, $y\in[1,16]$:
- Lower bound $(5x-13)/12 = 1$ when $x=5$; for $x<5$ it is clipped to $y=1$.
- Upper bound $(5x+13)/12 = 16$ when $x=35.8>35$; so no upper clipping occurs in $[1,35]$.

**Region 1:** $x\in[1,5]$, width $= \frac{5x+13}{12}-1 = \frac{5x+1}{12}$.
$$\int_1^5 \frac{5x+1}{12}\,dx = \frac{1}{12}\left[\frac{5x^2}{2}+x\right]_1^5 = \frac{1}{12}\left(\frac{125}{2}+5-\frac{5}{2}-1\right)=\frac{1}{12}\cdot 64 = \frac{16}{3}.$$

**Region 2:** $x\in[5,35]$, width $= \frac{13}{6}$.
$$\int_5^{35}\frac{13}{6}\,dx = \frac{13}{6}\cdot 30 = 65.$$

**Strip area** $= \frac{16}{3}+65 = \frac{211}{3}$.

**Sanity check.** The diagonal segment inside $\mathcal{R}$ runs from $(2.4,1)$ to $(35,14.58)$, length $\approx 35.3$; strip width $2$ gives $\approx 70.6$, consistent with $211/3\approx 70.33$ (slightly less due to end-clipping). ✓

**Probability.** Complement area $= 442 - \frac{211}{3} = \frac{1115}{3}$.
$$P = \frac{1115/3}{442} = \frac{1115}{1326}.$$

Check $\gcd(1115,1326)$: $1115=5\cdot 223$ and $1326=2\cdot 3\cdot 13\cdot 17$, so $\gcd=1$.

Thus $m=1115$, $n=1326$, and
$$m+n = \boxed{2441}.$$
